notes: Gap-fill plan for free-tier religious-education subject (school_id NULL, id 8efd391b-1981-46a2-a22f-0baf45925c2b).

Existing units (sort_order 1-8) MUST NOT be touched: christianity-beliefs, christianity-practices, islam-beliefs, islam-practices, theme-a-relationships, theme-b-religion-life, theme-d-peace-conflict, theme-e-crime-punishment.
Adds the 5 missing religions (Buddhism, Catholic Christianity, Hinduism, Judaism, Sikhism) each as Beliefs + Practices units of 4 lessons, plus the 2 missing themes (C and F) of 3 lessons each.
body_class follows the existing slug-based pattern (unit-{slug}) used by units 1-8 — NOT a numeric pattern.
accent_badge is the translucent <accent>33 form per memory rule, even though existing units 1-8 use solid pastel badges (those are legacy and out of scope for this gap-fill).

Christianity + Catholic Christianity is a prohibited combination at the AQA assessment layer (see spec section 2.1 / 3.1.3), but BOTH are valid options for schools to teach individually, so we ship both.

article_units.name: Buddhism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The Dhamma, the Buddha and the Four Noble Truths

lessons.title: The Dhamma and the Three Marks of Existence
lessons.description: The concept of Dhamma, dependent arising and the three marks of anicca, anatta and dukkha.

lessons.title: The Human Personality and Human Destiny
lessons.description: Theravada and Mahayana views on the self, including the Five Aggregates, sunyata, Buddhahood, Arhat and Bodhisattva ideals.

lessons.title: The Buddha and the Four Noble Truths
lessons.description: The Buddha's life of luxury, the Four Sights, ascetic life and Enlightenment, and the Four Noble Truths.

lessons.title: The Eightfold Path and Buddhist Ethics
lessons.description: The Threefold Way (sila, samadhi, panna), the Five Moral Precepts, kamma, karuna, metta and the Six Perfections.

article_units.name: Buddhism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: Worship, meditation, festivals and the moral life

lessons.title: Places of Worship and Puja
lessons.description: Temples, viharas, gompas and shrines; Buddha rupa, artefacts, offerings; the role of puja in home and temple.

lessons.title: Meditation: Samatha, Vipassana and Visualisation
lessons.description: Different aims and methods of Buddhist meditation including mindfulness of breathing, zazen and visualisation of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

lessons.title: Death, Funeral Rites and Festivals
lessons.description: Ceremonies and rituals associated with death and mourning in Theravada, Japan and Tibet; the festivals of Wesak and Parinirvana Day.

lessons.title: Ethics in Daily Life: Precepts and Perfections
lessons.description: How the Five Moral Precepts, kamma, karuna, metta and the Six Perfections shape Buddhist daily life.
section_markers: do not take what is not given

article_units.name: Catholic Christianity: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The Trinity, creation, incarnation, redemption and life after death

lessons.title: The Trinity and the Nicene Creed
lessons.description: One God as a Trinity of persons — Father, Son and Holy Spirit — as expressed in the Nicene Creed and the Council of Nicaea.

lessons.title: Creation and the Dignity of the Human Person
lessons.description: Genesis 1 and 2 accounts of creation, the dignity of human beings, humanity's relationship with creation and different Christian beliefs about creation.

lessons.title: Incarnation and Redemption
lessons.description: Jesus as fully God and fully human, and the significance of his life, death, resurrection and ascension for salvation and grace.

lessons.title: Life After Death and the Seven Sacraments
lessons.description: Catholic beliefs about resurrection, judgement, heaven, hell and purgatory, and the names, meanings and effects of the seven sacraments.

article_units.name: Catholic Christianity: Practices
article_units.subtitle: Prayer, popular piety, pilgrimage and the work of the Church

lessons.title: Prayer and Popular Piety
lessons.description: Formal and informal prayer, the Lord's Prayer, the Rosary and the Stations of the Cross.

lessons.title: Pilgrimage and the Funeral Rite
lessons.description: The role and importance of pilgrimage including a place of Roman Catholic pilgrimage, different Christian views about pilgrimage, and the funeral rite and its significance.

lessons.title: Catholic Social Teaching: Loving Our Neighbour
lessons.description: The duty to love our neighbour locally, nationally and globally, expressed through Gaudium et Spes, justice, peace and reconciliation, and the work of CAFOD, Trocaire and Missio.

lessons.title: Mission, Evangelism and Catholic Charities
lessons.description: Mission and evangelism for Catholics today; the aims and importance of the SVP and either Corrymeela or Pax Christi.
section_markers: Society of Saint Vincent de Paul

article_units.name: Hinduism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: Brahman, the divine, atman and the four aims of human life

lessons.title: Brahman and the Three Features of the Divine
lessons.description: Different Hindu understandings of Brahman as ultimate reality (nirguna and saguna), and the three features of the divine — non-personal, within the heart and as a personal loving God.

lessons.title: The Tri-murti, Deities and Avatars
lessons.description: Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; male and female deities including Ganesha, Lakshmi, Hanuman and Saraswati; the concept of avatar including Krishna and Rama.

lessons.title: Atman, Samsara, Karma and Moksha
lessons.description: The eternal inner self (atman), the cycle of birth and death (samsara), the law of karma and types of liberation (moksha); free will and responses to suffering.

lessons.title: The Four Aims of Life and Dharma
lessons.description: The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama and moksha — and the meaning of dharma, sanatana dharma and varnashrama dharma.

article_units.name: Hinduism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: Worship, festivals, the four yogas and pilgrimage

lessons.title: Worship at Home and the Mandir
lessons.description: Places of worship — home, temple, outdoors, the space of the heart — and forms of worship including havan, puja, arati, darshan, bhajan, japa and mantra; differences between Shaivism and Vaishnavism.

lessons.title: Focuses of Worship and the Murti
lessons.description: Focuses and representations of the divine: many deities, one God, the guru and elders, holy land and rivers, sacred plants and animals, and the murti as a representation of God.

lessons.title: Festivals: Diwali and Holi
lessons.description: The origins, meaning and importance of Diwali and Holi for Hindus in Great Britain today.

lessons.title: The Four Yogas, Pilgrimage and Hindu Charities
lessons.description: Karma, jnana, astanga and bhakti yoga; pilgrimage including Varanasi and Kumbh Mela; Hindu environmental projects and charities promoting well-being and women's rights.

article_units.name: Judaism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: God, the Covenant, the mitzvot and the sanctity of life

lessons.title: The Nature of God and the Shekhinah
lessons.description: God as One, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge — loving and merciful — and the divine presence (Shekhinah).

lessons.title: Life After Death and the Messiah
lessons.description: Jewish beliefs about judgement, resurrection and life after death; the nature and role of the Messiah and different views on the Messiah's importance.

lessons.title: The Covenant: Abraham, Moses and the Promised Land
lessons.description: The promised land and the Covenant with Abraham (Genesis 12:1-3); the Covenant at Sinai, the role of Moses and the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1-17).

lessons.title: Moral Principles, Mitzvot and Pikuach Nefesh
lessons.description: Justice, healing the world, charity and kindness; the sanctity of life and Pikuach Nefesh; the 613 mitzvot and the difference between mitzvot between man and God and between man and man.

article_units.name: Judaism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: The synagogue, Shabbat, family rituals and festivals

lessons.title: The Synagogue and Public Worship
lessons.description: The importance, design and features of the synagogue (bimah, aron hakodesh, ner tamid); differences between Orthodox and Reform synagogues; public acts of worship including the Amidah.

lessons.title: Shabbat, Home Worship and Sacred Texts
lessons.description: Shabbat in the home and synagogue; private prayer and worship in the home; the Tenakh and Talmud and their use in daily life.

lessons.title: Family Life: Birth, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, Marriage and Mourning
lessons.description: Brit Milah, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, the marriage ceremony and mourning rituals.

lessons.title: Dietary Laws and Festivals
lessons.description: Kosher and trefah, the separation of milk and meat, and different Jewish views about dietary laws; the festivals of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Pesach.

article_units.name: Sikhism: Beliefs and Teachings
article_units.subtitle: The Mool Mantra, mukti, equality and the priority of sewa

lessons.title: The Nature of God and the Mool Mantra
lessons.description: The content and significance of the Mool Mantra (Guru Granth Sahib 1a); God as Creator, shown in and through the universe and as separate from it.

lessons.title: Human Life, Sikh Virtues and Mukti
lessons.description: Human life as an opportunity to unite with God; the development of Sikh virtues; karma, rebirth, mukti and the five khands; the barriers to mukti and the goal of being gurmukh.

lessons.title: The Oneness of Humanity and Equality
lessons.description: The oneness of humanity, complete equality including the equality of women; equality expressed in the lives of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh, in the Guru Granth Sahib and in Sikhism today.

lessons.title: Sewa and the Sangat
lessons.description: The importance of sewa (service) — physical (tan), mental (man) and material (dhan) — and the role and importance of the sangat (religious community).

article_units.name: Sikhism: Practices
article_units.subtitle: The gurdwara, langar, festivals and the Khalsa

lessons.title: The Gurdwara: Worship and Community
lessons.description: Religious features of the gurdwara including the palki and takht; the role of the gurdwara within the Sikh community; the role of prayer in the home.

lessons.title: Akhand Path, Langar and Nam Japna
lessons.description: The role and importance of the akhand path; langar as an expression of sewa; meditating on the name of God (nam japna) in daily life and in the gurdwara.
section_markers: meditating on the name of God

lessons.title: Festivals, Birth and Naming Ceremonies
lessons.description: Vaisakhi, Divali and Gurpurbs (including Guru Nanak's birthday); birth and naming ceremonies; the importance of historic gurdwaras including the Golden Temple at Amritsar.

lessons.title: Amrit Sanskar, the Khalsa and the Five Ks
lessons.description: The initiation ceremony (Amrit Sanskar), the meaning and importance of the Khalsa, the five Ks, and the perspectives of sahajdhari and amritdhari Sikhs; the names Singh and Kaur.

article_units.name: Theme C: The Existence of God & Revelation
article_units.subtitle: Philosophical arguments for and against God, and the nature of revelation

lessons.title: Arguments For the Existence of God
lessons.description: The Design argument, the First Cause argument and the argument from miracles, including their strengths, weaknesses and an example of a miracle.

lessons.title: Arguments Against the Existence of God
lessons.description: Evil and suffering as an argument against God's existence, and arguments based on science against the existence of God.

lessons.title: Revelation: Visions, Miracles and Nature
lessons.description: Special revelation including visions and an example of a vision; enlightenment and general revelation through nature and scripture; ideas about the divine from these sources, and challenges to their value.

article_units.name: Theme F: Religion, Human Rights & Social Justice
article_units.subtitle: Equality, prejudice, freedom of religion, wealth and poverty

lessons.title: Human Rights, Equality and Freedom of Religion
lessons.description: Prejudice and discrimination in religion; the status and treatment of women and those in same-sex relationships; equality, freedom of religious expression and human rights with the responsibilities they bring.

lessons.title: Social Justice and Racial Discrimination
lessons.description: Social justice; racial prejudice and discrimination, including positive discrimination, and ethical arguments based on equality and justice.

lessons.title: Wealth, Poverty and the Uses of Money
lessons.description: Right attitudes to wealth, the duty to tackle poverty, exploitation including fair pay, excessive interest and people-trafficking; the responsibilities of those in poverty and the role of charity.
section_markers: giving to those living in poverty
